text.p: The Algerian parliament adopted a government minibudget on Monday, raising forecast total revenue for 1997 to 881.5 billion dinars ($15.74 billion) and spending to 946.22 billion dinars ($16.89 billion).
The official Algerian APS news agency said parliament passed the supplementary budget without changing the government proposals, which included a 15-billion dinars housing allocation.
Under the new finance law, the forecast budget deficit will be cut to 64.72 billion dinars ($1.15 billion) in 1997 from an original 84.70 billion dinars ($1.51 billion).

Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui told parliament, passing its first finance law since the country's first multiparty assembly was elected last June 5, "this is a good sign for a new start for the work of the pluralist national people's assembly."

The minibudget is based on an oil price of $18 a barrel, with income from oil and gas exports set at $12.5 billion for the year, up $1.0 billion from the original budget forecast. That forecast was based on an oil price of $17.50 a barrel.
The government readjusted the budget after revenue figures were affected by increased crude oil prices and a buoyant dollar. Imports have also been held down.
Expenditure was hit by salary increases for civil servants, subsidies for the country's retirement fund, underwriting credits to state-owned firms and spending on next October's local elections.

Official figures showed the volume and value of the country's oil and gas exports rose 7.9 percent and 13.1 percent, respectively, in the first five months of 1997 compared to the same period in 1996.
Algeria's oil and gas exports, which provide more than 90 percent of its foreign currency, totalled $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from the previous year.
Algeria, an Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) member, has a quota of 750,000 barrels per day. The country also exports about 30 billion cubic metres of gas a year.
